# Noisy physical token versus random starts: exact two-check comparison

2026-11-01. **Positive comparator result on the actual finite device.** The noisy physical token removes the dilution tradeoff for this two-check example. This is neither a full-network scheduling theorem nor a noisy-qudit memory threshold.

## Results: g=gamma=handoff rate=1

Private 12-level apparatus for each of ZZ and XX; one shared physical token bit. All entries below are per check, with symmetry numerically verified. Token preparation is enabled only for the owner in PARK, at rate 1. Random-start preparation ignores ownership, at the listed pump rate; it retains exactly the same additional DONE dwell and handoff hardware.

| scheme | pump | token X-flip rate | retained wrong (p=0) | retained wrong (p=.001) | report flux |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| token | 1 | 0 | <1e-15 | .00100000 | .06666667 |
| token | 1 | .0001 | .0000662797 | .00106615 | .06668608 |
| token | 1 | .001 | .000659917 | .00165860 | .06686014 |
| token | 1 | .01 | .00632301 | .00731037 | .06853785 |
| random | .1 | arbitrary, decoupled | .06399953 | .06487153 | .06030146 |
| random | .01 | arbitrary, decoupled | .00998576 | .01096579 | .00938853 |

Total two-check report flux is twice the last column. In particular, at token noise .001, the physical-token source has both better accuracy and higher throughput than either specified random-start baseline. This comparison does not claim random scheduling has been globally optimized over all possible controllers.

The increase of token flux with token noise is NOT a quality improvement: it accompanies unintended concurrency and more wrong reports. Probability both probes are active is approximately 0, .000161885, .00161351, .0156203 as token noise runs through the four values. It is .115249 and .00277776 for the two random baselines.

At zero noise, the ideal prediction is confirmed exactly to floating-point accuracy: each extraction takes mean 5.5 for two driven stages plus readout, one unit for launch, and one for handoff. Alternating ownership gives per-check flux 1/[2(5.5+1+1)]=1/15. No overlap floor remains.

# Actual resonant two-check source: finite-cell numerical receipt

2026-11-01. **Positive finite-cell test, not a uniform graph theorem or a practical memory threshold.** No external source access or hardware actions. This is the resonant sequential source, NOT the off-resonant Raman latch.

## Main result

Two overlapping checks ZZ and XX on the same two data qubits, with private 11-level apparatus each, have the following exact-Lindbladian numerical results at g=gamma=1 and pure plus preparation. Columns refer to either check; symmetry was checked, not assumed.

| pump r | retained cache wrong | per-check report flux | positive Poisson price range | isolated flux |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| .001 | .00105851993 | .000994528734 | 1011.291058 | .000994530085 |
| .01 | .0100762664 | .00947750342 | 111.284619 | .00947867299 |
| .05 | .0414867547 | .0391329715 | 31.2652664 | .0392156863 |
| .1 | .0679022374 | .0641489674 | 21.2554088 | .0645161290 |

Total pair report rate is TWICE the displayed per-check rate. Two isolated sources at the same r have total rate twice the isolated column. Pair/isolated per-check flux ratio declines only to approximately .9943 at r=.1, while wrong-cache probability reaches approximately .0679: throughput alone would miss the dominant effect.

With a physical convex minus-preparation branch p=.001, retained wrong values become .00205640289, .0110561139, .0424037812, .0687664329, respectively. Flux is unchanged in these examples. For comparison, an isolated source has retained wrong exactly p, within floating-point error.

The low-duty data support an approximately O(r) overlap error for THIS pair, with no high-order Raman slowdown. They do not establish a uniform-degree coefficient or prove a general asymptotic law. No arbitrary noise threshold or independent progress process was assumed.

## Actual model and gauge verification

Each apparatus basis is

    idle; g1,0 g1,1; e1,0 e1,1; g2,0 g2,1; e2,0 e2,1; final,0 final,1.

Each gate uses H_j=sum_b |e_j,b><g_j,b| tensor P_j^b+h.c. The separate stage jump is the COLLECTIVE sum_b |g_next,b><e_j,b|, with last target final. Probe coherence is not measured by this jump. Preparation jumps are sqrt(r(1-p))|g1,+><idle| and sqrt(rp)|g1,-><idle|. Readout jumps are |idle><final,s_X|, and the classical cache is overwritten with s. These are the actual generator ingredients, not effective op
